text:
IncidentBot: detected spike in 5xxs and tail latency on /v1/embed (continuous-batcher) — alerting oncall
Maya Patel: seeing it in the dashboard too, KV-layer cache hit rate dropped from 98% -> 62% over last 7m. throughput ok but tail latency up.
Maya Patel: tagging @Jin Park since you’re oncall for continuous-batcher today
Jin Park: on it. which pool/region?
Maya Patel: us-west-2, serving-pool-c1 (dedicated). Affected model: open-embed-v2 quantized.
Jin Park: okay reproducing logs now. grabbing recent runtime metrics.
OpsBot: deploy queued: patch/contbatch-hotfix-177355 - author: k.rivera — awaiting approval
Kelsey Rivera: I pushed a minimal config guardrail earlier this week — maybe it interacted with max_batch_tokens. rolling back that guardrail is easy if we need.
Jin Park: logs show continuous-batcher is creating many small batches but KV cache is being invalidated frequently — evictions spike. suspect misconfigured max_num_seqs or batch token accounting leading to page overflow in KV evictor.
Arne Schultz: any customer-facing impact yet?
Maya Patel: CS reports 3 customers with increased errors and slower embeddings, one on enterprise dedicated. CS Bot pasted customer ids.
Customer Success Bot: Customer A (acct-423) reported 30% failure rate for embedding requests between 16:41-16:49 UTC.
Jin Park: ok immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce max_batch_tokens -> 2048 (was 4096) on the shard to reduce per-batch working set 2) cap max_num_seqs -> 8 (was 32) so batcher doesn't pack many sequences into one KV footprint 3) increase KV cache memory soft-limit for shard by 12% to avoid premature evictions 4) enable short grace TTL for hot prefixes (30s)
Kelsey Rivera: I can push the runtime-config change to the pool as a hotfix. doing canary to 10% first.
Maya Patel: also recommend bumping continuous-batcher timeout to avoid stragglers triggering many small batches — set token wait ms from 20 -> 50ms for now.
Jin Park: agree. longer token wait reduces small-batch thrash.
OpsBot: deploy started: hotfix/contbatch-config-177355 -> canary node set (10%).
IncidentBot: service status: degraded — embeddings /v1/embed elevated errors and p50/p95 latency increased. Not yet classified as outage.
Kelsey Rivera: canary looks green for 2 nodes at 16:54 UTC. metrics: KV hit% up to 87% on canary, p95 latency down ~28%.
Jin Park: rolling to rest of pool now. patch command:
```
rbac apply runtime-config --pool serving-pool-c1 --set max_batch_tokens=2048,max_num_seqs=8,token_wait_ms=50,kv_soft_limit=1.12
```
Jin Park: issuing rollout with gradual 25% increments. monitoring logs and evictions.
Maya Patel: noting customer impact in incident doc: embed failures peaked 10:16 UTC? (typo: 16:16) — will capture exact windows for postmortem.
Customer Success Bot: Customer B (acct-881) reported timeouts in the same window, flagged priority-high.
Arne Schultz: we should prepare a short status note for CS and some immediate remediation text customers can use (retry/backoff).
Kelsey Rivera: sending templated message to CS: "We're aware of elevated embedding errors in us-west-2. We're rolling a configuration hotfix; recommend exponential backoff retries (start 200ms). We'll update in 15m."
Jin Park: rollout complete at 16:58 UTC. observability: global KV eviction rate down 73%, cache hit rate recovered to ~94%, errors returning to baseline.
IncidentBot: auto-check: p95 latency back to SLA target on canary and rolled nodes.
Maya Patel: great — please keep an eye on the enterprise customer and whether they see any residual failures.
Jin Park: reached out to Customer A via CS, asked for logs/timestamps; also requested they retry.
Kelsey Rivera: I opened a quick PR to add a guardrail test in CI to validate changes to max_num_seqs and batch token accounting won't exceed shard memory budget. PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8921
Arne Schultz: handoff note — I'm going to take over monitoring for the next 2 hours, Jin please add anything else to the incident doc before you drop from rotation.
Jin Park: adding quick root-cause hypothesis to doc: recent change to batching cost estimator (PR #8860) undercounted token footprint for quantized embedding model; combined with aggressive max_num_seqs allowed large KV working sets -> eviction storm -> cache blowup -> many small batches -> tail latency and 5xxs.
Jin Park: mitigation steps we did: reduced max_batch_tokens, capped max_num_seqs, increased kv soft limit, increased token_wait_ms. Long-term fixes: revert faulty estimator or change estimator to include KV footprint multiplier; add unit/regression tests; add runtime guardrail rejecting configs that exceed shard memory.
Maya Patel: going to update incident channel and start a brief postmortem doc. Will include customer impact timelines and prepare a draft communique for enterprise customers.
IncidentBot: incident status changed: mitigated -> monitoring.
OpsBot: deploy complete and tagged hotfix/contbatch-config-177355. changelog: runtime config adjustments.
Customer Success Bot: Customer A confirms retries succeeded after 17:02 UTC, error rate back to normal.
Arne Schultz: closing notes before handoff: we should schedule a follow-up to run load tests exercising quantized models with large seq counts so we don't regress again. adding to eng-runtime backlog.
Maya Patel: +1. Jin — great triage. I'm putting ownership of the postmortem on Eng-ML + Eng-Runtime.
Jin Park: thanks all. I'll add the full logs, exact hit/eviction graphs, and the command history to the incident doc before EOD.
Maya Patel: handing off to Arne for monitoring window.
Arne Schultz: taking over. if anyone sees a regression ping me directly. :eyes:
Maya Patel: thanks team :thumbsup:
